{{short description|Swiss mathematician}}
'''Kurt Strebel''' (20 April 1921 – 26 October 2013) was a Swiss mathematician, specializing in [[geometric function theory]].

==Education and career==
Strebel was born on 20 April 1921 in [[Wohlen, Aargau]]. received in 1953 his PhD from the [[University of Zurich]] under [[Rolf Nevanlinna]] with thesis ''Über das Kreisnormierungsproblem der konformen Abbildung'' (On the circle normalization problem of conformal mapping).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=57470}}</ref> From 1953 to 1955 he was at the Institute for Advanced Study and at Stanford University. He became a professor at the [[University of Fribourg]] in 1955 and then successor to Nevanlinna at the University of Zurich in 1963.

Strebel founded the Nevanlinna Colloquium in Zürich (later also elsewhere) with another of Nevanlinna's former students, the professor Hans Künzi, to maintain contacts with Nevanlinna.<ref>{{cite book|author=Strebel, Kurt|editor-first1=Bruno |editor-first2=Christine |editor-first3=Viktor |editor-last1=Colbois |editor-last2=Riedtmann |editor-last3=Schroeder |chapter=Rolf Nevanlinna in Zurich|title=mathch/100|publisher=European Mathematical Society|year=2010|pages=471–485|doi=10.4171/089|isbn=978-3-03719-089-0|chapter-url=http://www.ems-ph.org/books/show_abstract.php?proj_nr=120&vol=1&rank=21}}</ref> The Nevanlinna Colloquium is usually held in Europe and covers most of classical complex analysis.<ref>{{cite book|title=Lipa's Legacy: Proceedings of the Bers Colloquium, October 19–20, 1995|page=vii|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=u9gaCAAAQBAJ&pg=PR7|isbn=9780821806715|last1=Dodziuk|first1=Józef|last2=Keen|first2=Linda|year=1997 |publisher=American Mathematical Soc. }}</ref>

In 1977 Strebel was elected a member of the [[Finnish Academy of Sciences]]. He was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1974 in Vancouver.<ref>Strebel, Kurt. "On quadratic differentials and extremal quasi-conformal mappings." In Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, vol. 2, p. 223. Canadian Mathematical Congress, 1975.</ref>

He died on 26 October 2013 in [[Zürich]]. Named in his honor is the Strebel differential in the [[Teichmüller theory]].

==Strebel differential==
{{blockquote|{{underline|Definition}} A [[meromorphic]] [[quadratic differential]] is a Strebel differential if the union of its [[Compact space|noncompact]] [[foliation|leaves]] forms a set of [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]] 0.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Tynan, Philip|title=Explicit Examples of Strebel Differentials|eprint=0910.4752|year=2009|class=math.DG}}</ref>}}
